sentences.text: :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 06112020 at about 8.40 a.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding in a two wheeler Honda Diyo motor cycle bearing No.KA40EE2187 near Chennabyregouda stadium in Hosakote Town, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Canter bearing No.KA53D4220 drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's vehicle from behind.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Silicon City hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to MVJ Medical College & Research, wherein he was treated as an inpatient He has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical treatment,
conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as labourer and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the canter and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsels.
However, only respondent No.2 contested the petition by filing objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Canter.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further, it contended that the driver of canter had no M.S.Ganesh vs Akbar Pasha on 12 January, 2024
Indian
Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39378372/

2 valid and effective driving licence to drive and the owner of Canter knowingly entrusted the vehicle to a person who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and contended that at the time of alleged accident, the offending vehicle was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 06.11.2020 at about 8.40 a.m. near Channabyregouda stadium, Hosakote town,
Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of canter bearing No.KA 53D4220?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.2 and got examined PSI by name Sri.Raju C.M. as PW.1.
Through PW.1 and 2 documents at Ex. P.1 to 14 are got marked.
Petitioner also examined two witnesses as P.W.3 and PW.4.

Through them,
documents 15 to 22 got marked.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined the driver of offending canter as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 9. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 06112020 at about 8.40 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the canter bearing Regn.No.KA53D4220.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Canter.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.2 and he also examined three witnesses as P.W.1, PW3 and PW.4 and got marked 22 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P22.
P.W.2 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 are M.S.Ganesh vs Akbar Pasha on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39378372/

3 the True copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot Panchanama, PF, IMV report, Wound Certificate,
Indemnity bonds (2 in nos.), copy of Notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Reply to the notice and Charge sheet.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR along with Complaint shows that on the complaint lodged before Hosakote Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA53 D4220 for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the Spot panchanama drawn in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.3 is the PF.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Ex. P.6

is the copy of Indemnity bonds, Ex. P.7 is the copy of notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex. P.8 is the copy of reply to the said notice and Ex.P9 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Hosakote Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending Canter for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Ex. P.10 is Discharge summary, Ex. P.11 is the prescriptions and Ex. P.12 is the Medical bills.
Ex. P.13 is the Aadhar card.
Ex. P.14 is the Discharge summary.
Ex. P.15 is Authorisation letter.
Ex. P.16 is Case sheet.
Ex. P.17 to 19 are Xrays, Ex. P.20 is bills.
Ex. P.21 is Clinical notes and Ex.22 is Xray.
13. Further, P.W.2 examined a witness by name G.Arumugam, as PW.3 and Dr.R.Kantharaju as P.W.4 and they also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.

In addition,
the petitioner also got examined the PSI as PW.1.
PW.1 also reiterates the averments of the petition during his evidence.

During cross examination of PW.1, suggestions were made that though during the course of investigation it had come to his notice that the accident occurred as a result of negligence on the part of the petitioner herein, in order to help the petitioner to claim compensation the canter has been falsely implicated and charge sheet is submitted against the driver of canter.
Such suggestions are categorically denied by PW.1 14.
Further, the driver of canter got examined himself as RW.1 and he reiterated the Objection statement contentions in his chief affidavit.
In the cross examination, he deposed that he is ignorant of the fact of lodging of FIR against him and also regarding registration of charge sheet against him.
However, he admits to have not initiated any action against the rider of two wheeler i.e., the petitioner herein.
He denied the other suggestions of the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Canter by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 21 years.
He has produced Aadhar card to prove his age.
As per the Aadhar card i.e. Ex.P.13 the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 07.06.2000.
The accident taken place on 06.11.2020.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 20 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.

M.S.Ganesh vs Akbar Pasha on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39378372/
4 17.

Further, the petitioner has averred that he was doing labour work and was earning Rs.15,000/
per month.
No supportive documents are furnished to show that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/p.m.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence,
this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2020, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e.
15,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
19.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Multiple abrasion over face and 2. Lacerated wound over left ear.
3. Suspected pubic rami fracture.
4. Suspected fracture of left illiac bone.
5. Suspected blunt injury with anterior abdominal injury.
Further, the Doctor has opined that injury No.3 to 5 are grievous in nature and injury No.1 and 2 are simple in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

I COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
20.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
21.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 06.11.2020 to 11.11.2020.
Further, P.W.4 Dr.R.Kantharaju has also reiterated the same in his evidence.

22. Upon going through Ex.P.10 Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 06.11.2020 to 11.11.2020 at MVJ Medical college & Research Hospital i.e.,
totally for 6 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 6 days.

M.S.Ganesh vs Akbar Pasha on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39378372/
5 23.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500/ under this head (@ Rs.15,500/ per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
24.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
25. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 63 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.12 and 2 bills marked at Ex.P.20 which is totally amounting to Rs.60,048/.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same are acceptable.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
26. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and cannot work as earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.2 has deposed to that effect.

27. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. R.Kantharaju as P.W.4 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Clinical notes and xray at Ex.P.21 and 22.
He assessed total disability of left lower limbs at 33.08% and whole body disability at 11.02%.
28. In the crossexamination PW.4 has stated that he has not personally treated the petitioner.
He has also admitted that the fractures are united.
He also admits that there are no restrictions in the movements.
Apart from that there is also admission regarding the fact that the movements of knee and ankle are normal.
It is to be noted that PW.4 categorically admits that his assessment/calculation varies from the calculation provided in gazette.
He has denied the suggestion that without any disability to the Petitioner, he has given higher rate of disability to the Petitioner.

29. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 6% would be just and M.S.Ganesh vs Akbar Pasha on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39378372/
6 proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 6%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.2,00,880/ (Rs.15,500/ x 12 =
1,86,000/, Rs.1,86,000/x 18 x 6/100 =2,00,880/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,00,880/ which is rounded off to Rs.2,00,900/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
30.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 60,000/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 15,500/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.2,00,900/ Total Rs.3,56,400/ Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,56,400/with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

31. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA 53D4220.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
32. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.3,56,400/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

M.S.Ganesh vs Akbar Pasha on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39378372/
7
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 50%
of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
